claim: For Algorithm 1 (NMLM) of Zheng--Yang--Cao applied to any homogeneous linear system \(F(x)=Ax\) with \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) of full column rank, every nonterminal trial is accepted and the nonmonotone trust ratio satisfies \(\widehat r_k\ge 1\). Consequently the source damping-control variable is exact: \(\mu_k=\max\{\mu_0 4^{-k},m\}\), so the nonmonotone memory and all three acceptance thresholds do not affect the iterates on this class. Writing \(B=A^{\mathsf T}A\), the exact update is \(x_{k+1}=\lambda_k(B+\lambda_k I)^{-1}x_k\). Moreover, with \(\Lambda=\mu_0 e^{1/e}\), every nonzero iterate obeys the global contraction \(\|x_{k+1}\|\le q\|x_k\|\), where \(q=\Lambda/(\sigma_{\min}(A)^2+\Lambda)<1\). For the mathematical zero-tolerance continuation of the iteration, eventually \(\mu_k=m\) and \(\delta_k=1+1/\ln(k+e)\), and the quadratic error constant vanishes: \(\|x_{k+1}\|/\|x_k\|^2\to0\). Thus on full-column-rank linear systems the source algorithm has a Q-superquadratic tail in the explicit sense of a zero quadratic ratio, although its general local theorem specializes only to a quadratic bound when the error-bound and Jacobian Hölder exponents are both one.
integrity: The primary open full text was inspected at the damping rule, nonmonotone ratio, Algorithm 1 parameter updates, local-rate theorem, numerical-test description, and bibliography. The proof is independent and elementary; a standalone verifier checks the exact recurrence and representative finite computations. External comparison claims are limited to material actually inspected.
scientific_limitations: The affine theorem requires full column rank and exact LM solves. The Q-superquadratic statement concerns the mathematical zero-tolerance continuation; with the source's positive practical tolerance the method may stop before the asymptotic tail. No fixed convergence order strictly above two is claimed. The 2015 comparison paper was not available as lawfully inspectable full text, so an unindexed affine remark there remains a bibliographic risk.
title: Exact affine collapse and a vanishing quadratic constant in logarithmic-exponent NMLM
